name: Study wall
note: Haeckel radiolaria, Catlow’s water drops and Schmidt’s diatoms as one sepia ink on kraft. Mixed sources, one tone.
credits: Ernst Haeckel, Die Radiolarien (Rhizopoda radiaria) (1862); Agnes Catlow, A. Achilles, Drops of Water: Their Marvellous and Beautiful Inhabitants Displayed by the Microscope (1851); Adolf Schmidt, Atlas der Diatomaceenkunde (1890); Dr Alesha Sivartha, The Book of Life: The Spiritual and Physical Constitution of Man (1898)

name: Linen charts
note: Orra White Hitchcock’s 1828 geology classroom charts, natural colour, butted like a patchwork on linen.
credits: Orra White Hitchcock, Trap Vein in Clay Slate from Seil, Scotland (1828); Orra White Hitchcock, Sectional View of the Crust of the Earth (1828); Orra White Hitchcock, Granite Veins in Mica Slate from Williamsburg, Massachusetts (1828); Orra White Hitchcock, Granite Veins in a Boulder from Westhampton, Massachusetts (1828); Orra White Hitchcock, Geologic Trap (1828); Orra White Hitchcock, Diluvial Elevations and Depressions in Amherst, Massachusetts (1828)

name: Observatory
note: Trouvelot’s 1882 astronomical pastels on near-black. The ivory panel and coral button pick up Mars.
credits: Étienne Léopold Trouvelot, The Trouvelot Astronomical Drawings (1882)

name: Meander
note: Harold Fisk’s 1944 Mississippi meander maps in three columns. Already one palette, so only a light desaturation.
credits: Harold Fisk, Geological Investigation of the Alluvial Valley of the Lower Mississippi River (1944)

name: Cartographer
note: One plate, full bleed: the 1867 Sanborn map of Boston washed toward the paper so the panel stays legible.
credits: Daniel Alfred Sanborn, Sanborn map of Boston, Massachusetts (1867)

name: Paradiso
note: Caetani’s 1855 diagram of Dante’s Paradise, full bleed; the card sits inside the rings.
credits: Michelangelo Caetani, La Materia della Divina Commedia di Dante Alighieri Dichiarata in VI Tavole (1855)

name: Booth
note: Booth’s 1898–9 poverty map, sheet 7: Kensington through Belgravia to Pimlico, south of Hyde Park. Coloured streets edge to edge.
credits: Charles Booth (LSE Library scan), Maps Descriptive of London Poverty, 1898–9 (1899)

name: Booth north
note: Same sheet, the band north of the park: Notting Hill, Bayswater, Paddington and Marylebone. More red and blue, less gold.
credits: Charles Booth (LSE Library scan), Maps Descriptive of London Poverty, 1898–9 (1899)
